entry.evidence: The impacts on contaminant movement associated with spatio-temporally complex relationships between surface water and groundwater during such events in these regions are largely unknown.

sequences.source_document: Geris et al. 2022, published PDF and XML text

steps.action: Framed the knowledge gap on how extreme rainfall and flooding mobilise contaminants through surface water-groundwater interactions in semi-arid regions, and set three objectives.
steps.quote: We specifically addressed the knowledge gap on processes underpinning the spatio-temporal dynamics of water quality and contaminants

steps.action: Took the February 2017 extreme rainfall and flood in the Gaborone catchment, which followed a five-year drought, as a naturally occurring condition to study.
steps.quote: these conditions at the Gaborone catchment area provided an opportunity to study the effects of heavy rainfall on water resources

steps.action: Assembled CHIRPS rainfall, Department of Water Affairs reservoir storage and borehole levels, and two new EC and level loggers placed downstream of landfills. Took 285 water samples at 27 sites on 13 occasions from April 2017 to May 2018 and analysed them for stable isotopes, major ions, trace metals and TOC.
steps.quote: A total of 285 water samples were taken on 13 sampling occasions across the study period

steps.action: Acquired time-lapse ERT profiles (dipole-dipole, 48 electrodes, roll-along) next to the Otse landfill in May and July 2017, and inverted them with RES2DINV to map possible leachate plumes.
steps.quote: Apparent resistivity data were processed (removal of anomalous data associated to poor electrode contact) and inverted with RES2DINV v3.58

steps.action: Compared the 2016-2017 wet season total rainfall and maximum intensity, and the reservoir storage, against the 1981-2017 long-term record.
steps.quote: The 2016–2017 wet season received the second highest total rainfall (630 mm) since 1980

steps.action: Compared borehole water-table rises across high, moderate and low productivity aquifer types, and against depth to water table and distance to the thalweg.
steps.quote: In response to the heavy rainfall and flooding, we observed an average rise in water table across the boreholes of 8.79

steps.action: Interpreted the contrasting logger trends (Otse falling, Gaborone rising) as leakage from Gaborone Reservoir to downstream groundwater.
steps.quote: This indicates leaking of water from the reservoir to the groundwater in the overall downstream direction of the catchment.

steps.action: Compared isotope composition and d-excess between groundwater, reservoirs and streams, and inferred negligible recharge from evaporated surface water.
steps.quote: groundwater recharge contributions from fractionated surface water sources were undetectably small or non-existent

steps.action: Compared concentrations with WHO drinking-water guidelines, then compared mean, peak, timing and trend patterns across sites, including a link between concentration and isotope enrichment in surface waters.
steps.quote: There was a more general trend within surface waters (i.e. streams and reservoirs) whereby concentration of water quality indicators increased with heavy isotope enrichment

steps.action: Compared EC and contaminant trends upstream (Otse, G3) and downstream (Gaborone, G1) of Gaborone Reservoir.
steps.quote: At Gaborone, downstream of the reservoir, EC continued to increase throughout the observation period.

steps.action: Inferred from the inverted tomograms a low-resistivity leachate plume about 200 m long and down to about 50 m in May 2017, shrinking by July 2017.
steps.quote: suggests the existence of a plume of elevated groundwater solute concentrations associated with leaching and infiltration of contaminated water

steps.action: Checked the interpreted ERT lithology (alluvial clay over sandstone) against geological logs from the nearest documented boreholes.
steps.quote: These interpreted lithologies are confirmed by borehole geological logs

steps.action: Derived a regional hydrogeological conceptual model along a ~100 km transect, integrating all data types with existing maps and monitoring data.
steps.quote: Fig. 9 summarises our regional conceptual hydrogeological understanding along a key transect of the Gaborone catchment

steps.action: Refined the conceptual model into local schematics of water quantity and quality responses for the flood, the recession and the following wet season.
steps.quote: Fig. 10 then further refines our conceptual understanding of water level and water quality responses

steps.action: Drew on published expectations: recharge in arid zones occurs only during or shortly after heavy rain (Scanlon; Taylor), and nested groundwater flow follows the Tothian model.
steps.quote: consistent with what is expected for regionally nested groundwater flow systems under arid (low recharge) conditions

steps.action: Compared the isotope and topography-controlled water-table patterns with these published expectations and found them consistent.
steps.quote: This supports the model that recharge in these environments only occurs during or shortly after heavy rains

steps.action: Checked the inferred reservoir-driven recharge against isotope data (G1 similar to R1-R3). The isotopes supported it but were not variable enough to confirm it.
steps.quote: The role of Gaborone Reservoir in recharging subsurface water resources downstream was therefore supported by the isotope data.

steps.action: Set aside pollution as the cause of the high Mn concentrations, in favour of natural dolostone geochemistry and weathering.
steps.quote: although rather than polution (Hem, 1985), this was likely associated with bedrock geochemistry

steps.action: Proposed three rival mechanisms for rising groundwater contaminant concentrations (slow advection-dispersion, direct evapoconcentration, recharge by overconcentrated surface water) and left them unresolved.
steps.quote: Confirmation and better understanding of these processes would require more comprehensive groundwater monitoring both in space and time

steps.action: Checked the isotope-based inference about runoff generation (surface runoff on low productivity rocks, groundwater-fed main streams) against the independent water quality data.
steps.quote: The variations in water quality data confirm the isotope results

steps.action: Weighed recharge of evapoconcentrated reservoir water against landfill mobilisation as the cause of the rising contaminant trend at G1, and favoured landfill using the consistent Otse geophysics.
steps.quote: The geophysical survey observations near the Otse landfill showed consistent patterns.

steps.action: Kept local land use (farming, irrigation, landfill) as the dominant control on water quality patterns, while noting that the number of sites was too small for rigorous determination.
steps.quote: Land use appreared to be the dominant factor, although the number of accessible wells and surface water sampling points was too small

steps.action: Concluded that geology and topography dominantly control water hydrodynamic responses and interactions, and that groundwater-disconnected streams show higher and more strongly increasing contaminant concentrations.
steps.quote: geology and topography had a dominant control on spatial patterns in both surface and subsurface water hydrodynamic responses and interactions

Partly: levels and concentrations measured directly; plumes inferred by ERT inversion
Explain the controls on contaminant mobilisation and surface water-groundwater interaction
Informal rivals only, e.g. groundwater contamination mechanisms and the cause of the G1 trend
No distinct predictions derived for the rivals
Found: a live flood event, sampled from the recession onward

tree.answer: Partly: a smaller March 2018 flood and the following wet season gave a second, weaker case
Partly: consistency across data types (isotopes, chemistry, ERT, borehole logs)
Kept as best explanation; groundwater mechanisms left open

end.claim: Hydrogeological heterogeneity (geology and topography) controlled surface water-groundwater connectivity and water quantity responses to the 2017 flood, while local land use dominated water quality, with groundwater-connected streams showing consistently lower contaminant responses.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the post-flood multi-tracer campaign (285 samples for isotopes, ions and trace metals at 27 sites, plus loggers and ERT), no spatio-temporal comparison of connectivity and contamination would exist.

gates.evidence: Action: loggers and ERT were placed deliberately downstream of or next to landfills to capture expected leachate (p. 4-5: 'carefully chosen to represent sites downstream of unsealed landfill sites'), but the sampling network was general coverage rather than directed by a hypothesis. Claim: the conclusions faced only consistency checks across data types; for the reservoir recharge, isotope variability was 'not large enough to definitely confirm this' (p. 13). Registration: nothing is reported fixed before the data; the trend threshold (slope 0.1) and the ERT plume threshold (150 Ω.m, 'arbitrary') are stated without pre-specification.

imports.item: Agilent 7900 ICP-MS and MP-AES for trace metals and major ions
Los Gatos Research laser spectrometer for stable water isotopes
WHO drinking-water quality guidelines, and the median of national guidelines, as reference thresholds

novelty_claims.quote: In this generally data-sparce area, we collected a unique data set
their wider implementation to large scale study areas (>100 km2) is still lacking
by analysing the relationship between surface water and groundwater systems, where most studies would analyse these separately
our water quality data have revealed important new insights into the spatio-temporal water quality dynamics in a data-poor semi-arid region
This study has provided a unique dataset and analysis of the impact of extreme rainfall events on water quantity and quality

limits: Locations: the XML supplied contains only the abstract and figure captions, so body steps are located by printed page from the PDF. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The paper states that there are no pre-event or baseline water quality data, no flow monitoring, no NO3 analysis, no precipitation isotope sampling, and too few accessible wells for rigorous determination of controls. Sub-claims at weaker status: land use as the dominant water quality control (best_explanation, weakly supported); reservoir-driven recharge downstream (best_explanation, 'not large enough to definitely confirm'); the mechanism of rising groundwater contamination (no_conclusion; three rivals left open); the ERT plume extent (estimate, plume boundary set by an arbitrary 150 Ω.m threshold, no uncertainty stated). Composition is trace_series by inference: the event is recent rather than ancient, but the sampling began in the flood recession, so the flood itself is known only from its aftermath. Rivals are named but not tested by distinct predictions. Inference: the sampling design was largely coverage-driven, and the hypotheses were formed after the data.

disagreements.support: Their own measurements show most mean concentrations below WHO guidelines in the Gaborone catchment, apart from Mn and local arsenic.
disagreements.quote: In contrast to findings in more Eastern parts of the wider Limpopo basin

disagreements.support: High Mn is attributed to natural enrichment in dolostones and weathering, citing Franchi 2018, rather than to pollution.
disagreements.quote: although rather than polution (Hem, 1985), this was likely associated with bedrock geochemistry
